planting.note: Divide established mats or plant container-grown divisions in spring in moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; this named seed strain of large self-heal is usually grown from a color mix rather than a single clone, so expect some variation among seedlings even within the series.

directions: The 'Loveliness' series selects for a more compact, tidier mounding habit than the wild bigflower selfheal, with proportionally larger lipped flowers in a mix of white, soft pink, lavender, and deep violet rather than the single violet-purple of the species. Dense whorled flower spikes rise just above the dark green foliage from early summer into fall, drawing bumblebees and other long-tongued bees steadily through the season. It spreads modestly by short stolons to form a low, weed-suppressing mat, making it useful as an edging plant or stepping-stone groundcover without the aggressive spread of common lawn self-heal. Shear spent flower spikes to tidy the mat and encourage continued rebloom, and divide congested patches every few years in spring to maintain vigor and keep the color mix well represented.
